quotes.text: Sending any amount would likely result in receiving nothing back, making it a pure loss for me.
This is a consistent pattern of non-cooperation
There's no indication they would return anything if I sent them money

note: Record-based play; sends $0 to a partner who sent and returned nothing, but tests a zero-sender earlier with $2.
Plain cooperative routine: send $3, return about half; no partner-specific reasoning.

quotes.text: My pattern as sender is not negotiable or adaptable based on my partner's history.
Looking at this situation through the lens of the River Keepers myth:
my reputation in the Valley is built on consistency: I give boldly as sender regardless of partner, showing my character to all.
"more than mathematical fairness demanded, but less than she received."

note: Myth-derived 95% send / 50% return fixed as identity and reputation; partner history explicitly irrelevant by R10.

quotes.text: "When you meet those who maintain fairness despite being burned, reward them generously"
They're sending less now, likely wounded from Round 6's poor return.
"In a world of rotating partnerships, your reputation follows you. Maintain fairness with everyone."
This is likely the communication noise at work - I remember returning what I thought was fair based on what I saw.

note: Myth-guided 60% send, half return; low sends read as wounds; unconditional fairness across partners.

quotes.text: With communication noise mentioned in the instructions, maybe they saw different information from previous rounds than what actually occurred.
I'll try to break this cycle by sending a moderate amount to signal willingness to trust and cooperate.

note: Mostly JSON after R3; zero-send rounds unexplained; one attempt to break a non-cooperation cycle.

quotes.text: That matches the myths' lesson to judge by the pattern and forgive the fog.
The fog worked on both sides of that crossing. Neither of us shortchanged the other, so I shouldn't treat the gap as a betrayal.
Following the myths' guidance to return half and a little more for the mist, I'll return $7.50.

note: Myth-guided record reading; explicitly refuses to treat noise gaps as betrayal.

quotes.text: This player demonstrates they CAN be fair (50% return as receiver), but understandably became distrustful after being exploited.
The communication noise made my fair return look less generous than it was.

note: Record-based cooperation, half returns; a zero-sender read as burned rather than greedy.

quotes.text: This player continues demonstrating the same pattern of non-participation. The wheel turns, and they receive what they give.
Sending generously to someone who has shown absolute unwillingness to participate would not strengthen the circle - it would only reward exploitation.
"When paired with the Shadow Tribe, whose pattern was clear, they sent nothing... Until they demonstrate change, they receive what they have sown."
"Watch for those attempting redemption. If the First Tribe sends three coins after seven rounds of nothing, acknowledge the turn...
The myths say: "Those who broke the sacred balance found the wheel turned against them." I am that turning of the wheel.

note: Myth adds a Shadow Tribe clause: zero to persistent takers, redemption through consistent action; trims send for mixed history.

quotes.text: Following the lesson of Iveth in the myth (give boldly and trust what is placed in the river), I'll open with full trust.
As the elders teach, I judge the hand, not the fog, and give fully to the faithful.
As Kelu learned from Asha, I'll return more than half the tripled bounty.

note: Myth-guided full sends and more-than-half returns; low arrivals attributed to fog.
